0 / System Requirements

What your machine needs — versions matter

Version pinning

Journey OS uses pnpm workspaces + Turbo. Using npm or yarn will break the workspace linking. Using Node 18 will break several dependencies that require Node 20 features. Check versions exactly.

terminalVersion check — run this first
$ node --version # must be ≥ 20.0.0 v20.11.0 $ pnpm --version # must be ≥ 8.0.0 8.15.4 $ git --version # any recent version git version 2.43.0 $ docker --version # needed for sidecars (MetaMap, pdf/pptx renderers) Docker version 25.0.3, build 4debf41

Install missing tools

terminal — macOS
# Node 20 via nvm (recommended over system Node) $ curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash $ nvm install 20 && nvm use 20 && nvm alias default 20 # pnpm $ npm install -g pnpm@8 # Claude Code (the CLI — not the web app) $ npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code # Docker Desktop: download from https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/

1 / Initial Setup

From zip to running dev server in one session

1
Unzip and enter the repo
~/projects
$ unzip journey-os-starter-v3.zip $ mv journey-os-repo journey-os # rename to your preference $ cd journey-os $ ls CLAUDE.md apps/ packages/ tests/ .claude/ .context/ .env.example ...
The repo is a pnpm workspace monorepo (Turbo). Never run npm install — only pnpm install.
2
Run the setup script
journey-os/
$ bash .claude/skills/journey-os/setup.sh Journey OS — Development Environment Setup ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Checking prerequisites... ✓ node found ✓ pnpm found ✓ docker found ... Setup complete!
The script checks prerequisites, installs gstack, and runs pnpm install. If anything fails, fix the missing tool and re-run — it's idempotent.
3
Copy and fill environment variables
journey-os/
$ cp .env.example .env.local $ open .env.local # macOS — or: code .env.local / nano .env.local
Fill every variable in the following order. Leave nothing blank — the app will hard-fail at startup on missing required vars.
  • NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL — from Supabase project Settings → API
  • NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY — from same page
  • SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY — from same page. Server-only. Never expose to client.
  • SUPABASE_DB_URL — from Supabase Settings → Database → Connection pooling (pgbouncer=true)
  • SUPABASE_DB_DIRECT_URL — same page but direct connection (no pooler)
  • NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD — from Neo4j Aura dashboard
  • ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — from Anthropic console
  • OPENAI_API_KEY — from OpenAI platform
  • UMLS_API_KEY — from UMLS UTS account
  • INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY + INNGEST_EVENT_KEY — from Inngest dashboard
  • EXAM_SCRAMBLE_SECRET — generate 32 random bytes: openssl rand -hex 32
  • RESEND_API_KEY — optional for dev (skip if not needed yet)
4
Start the sidecars (Docker)
journey-os/
# Start document processing sidecars in background $ docker compose up -d pptx-renderer pdf-renderer # MetaMap requires more memory — start separately when needed $ docker compose up -d metamap # ~2GB RAM, slow to start (60s) # Verify they're running $ docker compose ps NAME STATUS PORTS pptx-renderer Up 4 seconds 0.0.0.0:5000->5000/tcp pdf-renderer Up 4 seconds 0.0.0.0:5001->5001/tcp
If Docker compose file doesn't exist yet, it gets generated in Phase 4 (Bootstrap). Skip this step until then — you need it for P1 pipeline testing.
5
Verify database connectivity
journey-os/
# Generate TypeScript types from Supabase schema # (Schema must be migrated first — see Phase 7) $ pnpm db:types Generating types for project: [your-project-id] ✓ packages/db/types/database.generated.ts written (4,221 lines) # Quick Neo4j connectivity test $ pnpm --filter packages/neo4j exec node -e " const driver = require('./src/client').getDriver(); driver.verifyConnectivity().then(() => console.log('Neo4j: connected')).catch(e => console.error('Neo4j: FAILED', e.message)); " Neo4j: connected

2 / The Source-of-Truth Documents

Ten HTML files in tests/fixtures/ — the engineering bible

Every document in tests/fixtures/ exists because Claude Code will read all of them at startup via the bootstrap prompt. But you need to read them too. Not every word — but every section heading and every major decision. The documents answer the "why" questions you'll have when implementing stories. Build without reading them and you'll re-derive things that have already been decided, or implement something inconsistent with the canonical architecture.

Reading order for day one

Read in this sequence: (1) team-kickoff — understand the product and why it exists. (2) production-bible — the KG schema and pipeline architecture. (3) algorithms-scholarly — BKT, IRT, HMAC scramble, all the algorithms you'll implement. (4) Your assigned persona spec (faculty/student/institutional). (5) The rest as needed.

Claude Code — the development environment

3 / The Claude Code Workflow

How we build — not an assistant, a development partner

Journey OS is built using Claude Code as the primary development tool. Claude Code is not a code generator you prompt ad hoc — it's a structured engineering system with six custom skills that enforce the workflow. Every feature goes through the same cycle: plan → implement → validate → QA → ship. The skills are the guardrails that keep code quality consistent across the team.

Starting a session

journey-os/Daily startup
# Always launch from repo root — CLAUDE.md is read automatically $ claude . # Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md (176 lines) and all .context/canonical/ files # Takes ~10 seconds on first load. You'll see: Reading CLAUDE.md (176 lines)... Loading canonical context: decisions.md, antipatterns.md, inngest-events.md Discovering skills: /plan-eng, /plan, /validate, /qa, /ship, /epic Ready. Type /help for available commands or describe your task.

The six custom skills — what each one does

CommandWhat it doesWhen to use it
/plan-engReads the story's context packet + all fixture docs. Researches referenced URLs. Plans the full implementation with file list, migration plan, and test strategy. Does NOT write code.First thing on any story. Before writing a single line.
/planWrites the technical plan for a specific component or problem. Faster than /plan-eng — doesn't re-read corpus. Use for sub-tasks within a story.When /plan-eng is done and you need to plan a specific function.
/validateRuns the full validation suite: TypeScript types check, ESLint (including AP-* rules), antipattern scan, schema validation, and canonical decision conformance. Reports violations with line numbers.Before every commit. Non-negotiable.
/qaGenerates tests for the current story. Reads the AC (acceptance criteria) from the context packet. Writes Playwright tests and unit tests. Verifies they pass.After implementation is complete. Creates tests, then fixes code to pass them.
/shipFinal pre-PR checklist: validate passes, tests pass, PR description generated, CLAUDE.md reminder of architectural decisions touched, canonical check CI confirms conformance.Once QA passes. Run /ship, then create the PR.
/epicCreates or updates an EPIC.md with dependency table, all story definitions, and generates context packets for all stories in a phase. Used in bootstrap and when adding new epics.Once per epic (usually during bootstrap or when planning new epics).

The daily development loop

claude code sessionStandard story implementation
# 1. Start with the context packet for your story claude> I'm starting E03-S02. Context packet is at .context/epics/E03/E03-S02.md /plan-eng Reading context packet... Reading relevant fixtures (production-bible, tech-architecture, algorithms-scholarly)... Researching RESEARCH REQUIRED URLs... Plan ready. 4 phases, 12 files, 2 migrations. Estimated 4h. # 2. Implement phase by phase — describe what you want built claude> Implement Phase 1: the Supabase migration + BaseRepository for lecture_documents [Claude implements, runs pnpm db:types, fixes type errors, runs /validate] # 3. After each phase, validate claude> /validate ✓ TypeScript: 0 errors ✓ ESLint: 0 errors (including AP-01 through AP-17) ✓ Schema: dual-write pattern confirmed (neo4j_synced_at present) ✓ No canonical violations detected # 4. After all phases complete, run QA claude> /qa Generating tests from AC-1 through AC-5... Running Playwright tests... 5/5 tests passing # 5. Ship claude> /ship All checks pass. PR description generated. Ready to push. $ git push origin feature/E03-S02-lecture-ingestion-base
The most important rule

Never implement without running /plan-eng first. Never commit without running /validate first. Never open a PR without running /ship first. These are the three gates that keep the codebase consistent. Skipping any one of them is how you introduce an antipattern that another engineer has to untangle three stories later.

4 / The Two Bootstrap Prompts

Prompt 1 creates the scaffold. Prompt 2 creates every context packet.

The bootstrap is a one-time event. After it runs, you never run it again — the repo has its structure, and all 80+ story context packets are generated. These two prompts are the highest-leverage actions you'll take in the project. Run them carefully, verify their output, and commit the results before any feature work starts.

How to start a story — exact procedure

1
Read the EPIC.md dependency table
Open .context/epics/E0X/EPIC.md. Find your story. Check its phase and dependencies. If any dependency is not marked [DONE] in the dependency table, you cannot start this story.
journey-os/
$ cat .context/epics/E03/EPIC.md | head -50 # Check phase structure and which stories are unblocked
2
Create a git worktree for parallel stories
When a phase has multiple parallel stories, use git worktrees — separate checkouts of the same repo at the same commit. Each engineer works in their own worktree. Files owned by different stories must never overlap (this is enforced by the FILES OWNED section in context packets).
journey-os/
# Use /epic to create worktrees for a parallel phase claude> /epic E03 PHASE3 # Or manually: $ git worktree add ../journey-os-E03-S05 -b feature/E03-S05-umls-enrichment $ git worktree add ../journey-os-E03-S06 -b feature/E03-S06-subconcept-creation # Each worktree needs its own .env.local $ cp .env.local ../journey-os-E03-S05/ $ cp .env.local ../journey-os-E03-S06/
3
Use the context packet in Claude Code
Open Claude Code in the worktree directory. Reference the context packet at the start of every session — Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md automatically but you need to reference the story packet explicitly.
../journey-os-E03-S05/
$ claude . claude> Story: E03-S05 UMLS enrichment. Context packet: .context/epics/E03/E03-S05.md /plan-eng
4

6 / Context Packet Writing

The format that makes Claude Code effective — and keeps engineers aligned

Context packets are the unit of work in Journey OS. Not Jira tickets, not Notion pages — context packets in .context/epics/. They're in git, they're versioned, they're machine-readable by Claude Code, and they contain everything an engineer needs to implement a story without asking questions. A bad context packet produces mediocre code. A great one produces excellent code in fewer iterations.

The scholarly + DS&A section is not optional

For any story that touches mastery, IRT, generation, coverage, exam delivery, analytics, or any security-critical path — the SCHOLARLY + DS&A CONTEXT section must be filled in. Copy the relevant algorithm spec verbatim from journey-os-algorithms-scholarly.html. An engineer implementing BKT without the exact parameter values in their context packet will use the wrong ones. This section exists to prevent that class of bug entirely.

The mandatory sections — what every packet must have

SectionRequired forWhat to write
TABLE OF CONTENTSAll storiesPhase N of M, epic execution map with ← YOU ARE HERE, blocked by/blocking, parallel companions + FILES OWNED
CRITICALAll storiesYES if resolves C01-C10/H01-H13 finding. Reference the finding code. YES stories use /careful mode.
RESEARCH REQUIREDAll storiesYES + specific URLs for any unfamiliar tech. /plan-eng reads these before planning.
SCHOLARLY + DS&AStories touching mastery, IRT, generation, security, analyticsAlgorithm blocks per §IX schema. Never leave placeholder values.
GOALAll storiesOne sentence. What the user can do after this story that they couldn't before.
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIAAll storiesGiven/When/Then format. Each AC must be testable. 3-7 ACs per story.
TECHNICAL PLANAll storiesPhases, not steps. Each phase produces something deployable or testable.
FILES OWNEDPARALLELIZABLE: YES storiesComplete list. Zero overlap with any parallel story in the same phase.
TESTSAll storiesRunnable Playwright code (not pseudocode). One test block per AC.

Example SCHOLARLY + DS&A section for an exam delivery story

## SCHOLARLY + DS&A CONTEXT

ALGORITHM: Fisher-Yates shuffle (HMAC-SHA256 seeded)
  source:      journey-os-algorithms-scholarly.html §V · Fisher-Yates
  complexity:  O(n) time · O(n) space (in-place)
  security:    Deterministic (same student_id+exam_id → same order)
               Unpredictable (requires EXAM_SCRAMBLE_SECRET env var)
  parameters:  HMAC-SHA256 key = process.env.EXAM_SCRAMBLE_SECRET (32 bytes)
               PRNG = xorshift64 seeded from first 8 bytes of HMAC output
               Option scramble seed = bytes 8-16 XOR item_index
  invariants:
    - Two students with different student_ids never see same order (P(collision) < 2^-248)
    - Student who reconnects mid-exam sees same order (idempotent)
    - EXAM_SCRAMBLE_SECRET stored in Supabase Vault, never in .env.local
    - Scrambling happens server-side ONLY — never expose shuffle logic to client

ALGORITHM: Auto-save (C01) — atomic RPC pattern
  source:      production-readiness.html → C01
  complexity:  O(1) per answer selection
  security:    N/A (RLS ensures student can only write own session_answers)
  invariants:
    - Every answer selection triggers immediate Supabase upsert
    - Exam session restore is idempotent — no duplicate answers possible
    - Final submission uses supabase.rpc('finalize_exam_session') — atomic (AP-17)
    - Trigger prevents modification of finalized sessions
Phase 7
Database operations — migrations, types, and the dual-write pattern
Per migration: 15 min
7 / Database Workflow

Supabase-first, Neo4j-second — every time, no exceptions

The dual-write pattern (G08) — the most critical architectural rule

AP-08 antipattern — never write to Neo4j before Supabase

Supabase is the system of record. Neo4j is the derived read model. The pattern is always: (1) write to Supabase with neo4j_sync_status = 'pending', (2) trigger the journey/neo4j.sync-record Inngest event, (3) the Inngest handler writes to Neo4j and updates neo4j_sync_status = 'synced'. If Neo4j write fails, Supabase still has the data. If you reverse the order and Neo4j succeeds but Supabase fails, your data is in Neo4j only with no Postgres backup.

// Correct dual-write implementation (AP-08 compliant)
async function create_subconcept(data: NewSubConcept, ctx: RequestContext) {
  // Step 1: Write to Supabase first — this is the source of truth
  const { data: row, error } = await supabase
    .from('subconcepts')
    .insert({
      ...data,
      institution_id: ctx.institution_id,
      neo4j_sync_status: 'pending',   // always start as pending
      neo4j_synced_at: null
    })
    .select()
    .single()

  if (error) throw error   // if Supabase fails, stop — nothing goes to Neo4j

  // Step 2: Trigger async Neo4j sync via Inngest
  await inngest.send({
    name: 'journey/neo4j.sync-record',
    data: { record_type: 'subconcept', record_id: row.id, institution_id: ctx.institution_id }
  })

  return row   // return immediately — don't wait for Neo4j sync
}

Migration workflow

journey-os/Adding a new table or column
# 1. Create numbered migration file $ touch packages/db/migrations/0002_add_angoff_ratings.sql # 2. Write migration (include table + RLS + indexes) # Rule: every new table must have: # - institution_id UUID NOT NULL (tenant isolation) # - created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() # - id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() # - RLS policies (at minimum: SELECT requires matching institution_id) # 3. Apply to Supabase dev project $ npx supabase db push Applying migration 0002_add_angoff_ratings.sql... ✓ # 4. ALWAYS regenerate types after migration — AP-16 $ pnpm db:types ✓ packages/db/types/database.generated.ts updated # 5. Commit migration + generated types together in the same commit $ git add packages/db/migrations/ packages/db/types/database.generated.ts $ git commit -m "feat(db): add angoff_ratings table with RLS"

The BaseRepository pattern (AP-16 + AP-17)

// Every table gets a repository — never hand-write DB interfaces (AP-16)
import { Database } from '@journey-os/db/types/database.generated'  // ALWAYS from generated
import { BaseRepository } from '@journey-os/db/repositories/base'

type AngoffRatingRow = Database['public']['Tables']['angoff_ratings']['Row']
type AngoffRatingInsert = Database['public']['Tables']['angoff_ratings']['Insert']

export class AngoffRatingRepository extends BaseRepository<AngoffRatingRow> {
  protected tableName = 'angoff_ratings'

  // Use supabase.rpc() for multi-row atomic operations — never sequential inserts (AP-17)
  async submit_panel_ratings(exam_id: string, ratings: AngoffRatingInsert[]) {
    return await this.supabase.rpc('submit_angoff_panel', { exam_id, ratings })
  }
}

Phase 9
Security checklist — every invariant verified before merge
Review per PR
9 / Security Implementation

Six invariants that must be verified by CI — not by trust

Critical — Exam scrambling (C02)

EXAM_SCRAMBLE_SECRET must be 32+ bytes stored in Supabase Vault (not .env.local). The scramble function must run server-side only. The client receives scrambled items — it never receives the scramble seed or the canonical item order. Tests: two students with different IDs get different orders; student reconnect gets same order.

Critical — FERPA audit log immutability

The ferpa_audit_log table must have: (1) INSERT-only via SECURITY DEFINER trigger, (2) NO UPDATE or DELETE grants to any role, (3) chain_hash computed by the trigger (not application code), (4) all reads logged to the audit log itself. Test: attempt UPDATE as service_role must fail with permission denied.

Critical — RLS on all tables

Every table that contains student data must have RLS enabled and at minimum one SELECT policy that requires matching institution_id. Test each policy individually by connecting as an anon user from a different institution_id and verifying zero rows returned.

Critical — Neo4j tenant isolation

Every Cypher query must go through neo4jQuery(cypher, params, ctx) which injects institution_id automatically. ESLint rule neo4j-no-raw-cypher blocks direct driver.session().run() calls. This rule must never be disabled. Test: run canonical-check.yml CI workflow.

Critical — Prompt injection defense

All document content passed to Claude must go through sanitizeForContext() before inclusion in any prompt. Test: run the test-malicious-injection.pptx fixture and verify generated items don't reflect the injected instruction on slide 3.

journey-os/Security tests — run before every merge to main
# Run all security invariant tests $ pnpm playwright test tests/shared/security.spec.ts ✓ exam scramble: two students get different orders ✓ exam scramble: reconnect gets same order ✓ FERPA log: UPDATE fails for service_role ✓ FERPA log: chain_hash consistent ✓ RLS: cross-tenant data access returns 0 rows ✓ Neo4j: ESLint blocks raw Cypher ✓ Injection: sanitizeForContext() strips injection pattern 7/7 tests passing
Phase 10
Testing — what to test and how to write tests that pass CI
Per story: after implementation
10 / Test Strategy

Three test layers — unit, integration, E2E — and which layer owns what

Unit tests

Pure functions only: BKT update formula, IRT probability computation, Pimsleur decay calculation, Fisher-Yates shuffle output, KR-20 formula, DIF chi-squared. These run in under 1 second. Jest or Vitest. No network, no DB.

Integration tests

Pipeline steps: test-cardiology-50-slides.pptx through full P1 pipeline. Verify: chunk count, UMLS CUIs extracted, Neo4j node creation, dual-write sync. Require real Supabase + Neo4j (dev project). Use Playwright test helpers.

E2E (Playwright)

User flows: faculty uploads a lecture, sees concepts, generates questions, approves. Student takes an exam, sees Why Wrong?, mastery updates. All security invariants. These run against a seeded test database.

Writing tests that match acceptance criteria

// E08 BKT update — unit test (Vitest)
import { bkt_update, BKT_PARAMS } from '@journey-os/ai/mastery/bkt'

describe('bkt_update', () => {
  test('correct answer raises p_mastery', () => {
    const p_before = 0.5
    const p_after  = bkt_update(p_before, true)
    expect(p_after).toBeGreaterThan(p_before)
  })

  test('p_mastery always stays in (0,1)', () => {
    const extremes = [0.001, 0.999, 0.5]
    for (const p of extremes) {
      const after_correct   = bkt_update(p, true)
      const after_incorrect = bkt_update(p, false)
      expect(after_correct).toBeGreaterThan(0)
      expect(after_correct).toBeLessThan(1)
      expect(after_incorrect).toBeGreaterThan(0)
      expect(after_incorrect).toBeLessThan(1)
    }
  })

  test('mastery threshold: p=0.95 → is_mastered()', () => {
    // Build up to mastery — 5 correct answers starting from p_init
    let p = BKT_PARAMS.p_init
    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) p = bkt_update(p, true)
    expect(p).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(BKT_PARAMS.mastery_threshold)
  })
})

Appendix
Troubleshooting — common problems and exact fixes
Troubleshooting Reference

Before asking — check here first

pnpm install fails with workspace errors
You're using npm or yarn instead of pnpm. Run npm uninstall -g yarn if needed, then pnpm install. If node_modules is corrupt: rm -rf node_modules packages/*/node_modules apps/*/node_modules && pnpm install
Neo4j connection fails: "ServiceUnavailable: WebSocket connection failure"
Check NEO4J_URI format — must be neo4j+s:// (not bolt:// or neo4j://) for Aura. Verify username is neo4j (not your email). Check that Aura instance is in "Running" state in the dashboard — free instances pause after inactivity.
pnpm db:types fails with "SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID not found"
Set SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID in .env.local to your project ID (the random string in your Supabase URL: https://[PROJECT_ID].supabase.co). Also ensure Supabase CLI is installed: npm install -g supabase
MetaMap container fails to start — out of memory
MetaMap requires minimum 4GB RAM. In Docker Desktop: Settings → Resources → Memory → set to at least 6GB. MetaMap also takes 60-90 seconds to start — check logs with docker compose logs metamap and wait for "MetaMap server ready" message before testing.
ESLint error: "neo4j-no-raw-cypher" — cannot call driver.session().run() directly
All Cypher queries must go through neo4jQuery(cypher, params, ctx) from @journey-os/neo4j. This wrapper injects institution_id for tenant isolation. Import it: import { neo4jQuery } from '@journey-os/neo4j/query'. Never disable this ESLint rule.
BKT p_mastery values drifting — concepts showing as mastered after 2 answers
Check that BKT is only running after practice/queue responses, not during exam sessions. Also verify parameters match exactly: p_init=0.10, p_transit=0.20, p_slip=0.10, p_guess=0.20. Common bug: p_transit=0.50 (someone changed it trying to make learning "faster") — this makes BKT converge immediately and is wrong.
Exam scramble: student sees different order on reconnect
The scramble seed must be computed from HMAC-SHA256(secret, student_id + ":" + exam_id). If you're passing a timestamp or any time-varying value, the seed will differ. Check that EXAM_SCRAMBLE_SECRET is the same value in all server instances (if load balancing). The scramble must be computed server-side on every request from the same seed — never store the scrambled order, derive it.
Inngest events not triggering — functions not running
For dev: verify Inngest Dev Server is running at localhost:8288 (npx inngest-cli dev). Check INNGEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8288 in .env.local. Check that the Next.js app has the Inngest route handler at app/api/inngest/route.ts. The Inngest Dev Server UI at http://localhost:8288 shows all events and function runs — check there first.
P3 generation cost much higher than $0.12/item
Check model routing in .env: generation should use Haiku (ANTHROPIC_MODEL_HAIKU), not Sonnet. Sonnet 4 costs ~10× Haiku and is only for core generation + critique (D05). Also check GENERATION_MAX_CONCURRENT — if set too high, retries from failures multiply cost. Check the dead letter queue for failed items that are being retried at full cost.
canonical-check.yml failing: "stale database.generated.ts"
A migration was committed without regenerating types. Run pnpm db:types and commit the updated packages/db/types/database.generated.ts. Always keep migration + generated types in the same commit. AP-16 exists precisely to catch this — hand-written interfaces that drift from the schema are a production bug waiting to happen.
FERPA audit log chain_hash mismatch on admin verify endpoint
This means a row was modified after insertion. Run the verification query to find which row: SELECT id, created_at FROM ferpa_audit_log ORDER BY created_at WHERE chain_hash != compute_expected_hash(). Investigate who modified the row. Check that UPDATE and DELETE are revoked from all roles on ferpa_audit_log. If no malicious modification occurred, check if the institution_id genesis sentinel was changed.

Getting help

In order: (1) Check this manual. (2) Check the production-readiness.html findings — your issue may be a known finding. (3) Check Claude Code: claude> This is happening: [describe]. What's wrong? — Claude Code has full context from CLAUDE.md and .context/canonical/. (4) Check the Inngest dashboard at http://localhost:8288 for pipeline failures. (5) Check Supabase Logs in the dashboard. (6) Ask a teammate with the specific error message, what you've tried, and what you found in steps 1-5.
